literature_basis_for_collective_coupling: L. L. Foldy, Phys. Rev. 67, 107 (1945): self-consistent multiple scattering of point scatterers
Z. Zeravcic, D. Lohse, W. van Saarloos, J. Fluid Mech. 680, 114 (2011): collective oscillations in bubble clouds
M. Lanoy, C. Derec, A. Tourin, V. Leroy, Appl. Phys. Lett. 107, 214101 (2015): secondary Bjerknes forces in bubble groups require the coupled response
Chin. Phys. B 22(1), 014304 (2013): higher bubble density suppresses the interaction force inside a cluster
M. Ida, arXiv:physics/0109005: sign reversal of the secondary Bjerknes force at close range
limitations: Collective coupling is a linear monopole (fundamental-only) closure: no translation coupling, no multipoles or non-spherical modes, higher harmonics isolated, no shell contact, fusion or breakup
Not calibrated against any experiment; the drift reversal of a dense cluster is a model prediction to test, not a finding
O(N^3) dense solve per force evaluation; fine for hundreds of bubbles, larger N needs an iterative or GPU solver
Other frequencies or radii may approach a collective resonance; the run fails at the singular guard instead of regularizing
Pretraining tolerances (1e-10 m residuals, rtol 1e-4) are tied to the observation scale; results are not admissible as frozen-tier evidence
No wall contact model; runs stop 2R from the lumen wall or end
Coarse 2.5/2.4/2.6 MHz field caches only; same cubic-cache interior restriction as HF/LF
not_implemented: Per-channel frequencies and GPU direct field computation with a linear response formula
Raising the frozen HF/LF 1500 Pa-equivalent cap (only the pretraining tier has its own 3000 cap)
Batched in-process parallel runs (runs were parallel processes)
Reduced-order deformation model and rigid-group integration
GPU kernels for the collective closure or the sparse contact step
Active phase control beyond the existing per-segment phases
